title: Comparative Religion
subject: Religious studies
blurb: Compare scriptures, core ideas, practices and histories across the world's major religious traditions.

rounds.title: Round 1: Founders, texts and canons
rounds.intro: Religious traditions preserve their teachings in sacred texts and collections. See if you can match each text to its tradition and its role.

questions.q: The word Tanakh is an acronym for which three sections of the Hebrew Bible?
choices: Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim
Torah, Talmud, Midrash, the three core rabbinic collections
Torah, Mishnah, Gemara
Law, Gospels, Epistles
questions.why: Tanakh stands for Torah (Teaching), Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings). Talmud, Mishnah and Gemara are later rabbinic works, not parts of the Tanakh.

questions.q: Which description fits a hadith?
questions.scene: A Muslim scholar cites a report of something the Prophet Muhammad said or did, traced back through a named chain of narrators.
choices: A commentary explaining the meaning of Qur'an verses
A report of the Prophet's words or deeds, with its chain of narrators
The psalms that Muslims believe were revealed to David
A legal ruling made within one school of Islamic law
questions.why: Hadith are reports about Muhammad, evaluated by their chain of transmission. Tafsir explains the Qur'an and fiqh is legal reasoning built on the Qur'an and hadith, so they are easy to confuse with it.

questions.q: The Pali Canon of Theravada Buddhism is called the Tipitaka, or 'three baskets'. Two baskets are Vinaya (monastic rules) and Sutta (discourses). What is the third?
choices: Tantra
Lotus Sutra
Abhidhamma
Dhammapada only
questions.why: The third basket is the Abhidhamma, a systematic analysis of mind and experience. The Dhammapada is a single book inside the Sutta basket, and the Lotus Sutra belongs to Mahayana collections, not the Pali Canon.

questions.q: Which scripture is this?
questions.scene: A gurdwara keeps a scripture on a raised seat under a canopy and treats it with the honor given to a living teacher. Its hymns include verses by poets such as Kabir and Farid, alongside those of the Sikh Gurus.
choices: The Bhagavad Gita
The Avesta
The Kitab-i-Aqdas of Bahá'u'lláh
Guru Granth Sahib
questions.why: Sikhs honor the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru, and it includes hymns by non-Sikh saints. The Gita is a Hindu text, the Avesta is Zoroastrian and the Kitab-i-Aqdas is a Bahá'í book.

questions.q: Which assignment of sources is correct?
questions.scene: Passage A: 'To govern by virtue is like the pole star, which keeps its place while all the other stars turn toward it.' Passage B: 'The Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao.'
choices: A: Analects; B: Dao De Jing
A is from the Dao De Jing; B is from the Analects
Both are from the Analects
A is from the Dao De Jing; B is from the Mencius
questions.why: Passage A is Analects 2.1, a Confucian text about moral leadership. Passage B opens the Dao De Jing, which says the ultimate Dao cannot be fully captured in words.

questions.q: The Avesta, whose oldest hymns (the Gathas) are attributed to Zarathustra, is the sacred collection of which tradition?
choices: Jainism
Sikhism
Manichaeism, the religion of Mani
Zoroastrianism
questions.why: Zoroastrians use the Avesta in worship, and the Gathas are its oldest layer. Manichaeism was a separate religion founded by Mani that borrowed some Persian themes.

questions.q: Hindu tradition often separates shruti ('heard' revelation) from smriti ('remembered' tradition). Which text is usually classed as smriti?
choices: The Rig Veda
The Upanishads, the Vedic philosophical texts
The Bhagavad Gita
The Brahmanas
questions.why: The Gita is part of the epic Mahabharata, so it is smriti. The Vedas, Brahmanas and Upanishads make up shruti, though many Hindus treat the Gita with equal reverence.

questions.q: Which statement about the Old Testament and Tanakh is accurate?
questions.scene: Books such as Tobit, Judith and Wisdom of Solomon appear in some Christian Bibles but not in the Hebrew Bible.
choices: Protestant Old Testaments match Catholic ones in contents, and both differ from the Tanakh in book count
The Tanakh includes Tobit and Wisdom, and Protestants removed them
Eastern Orthodox Bibles contain fewer Old Testament books than Protestant Bibles
Protestant Bibles follow the Hebrew canon; Catholic and Orthodox add deuterocanonical books
questions.why: Protestants generally use the Hebrew canon's contents, though arranged differently. Catholics and Orthodox include deuterocanonical books, and the Orthodox lists vary and are often the longest. The Tanakh does not include these books.

rounds.title: Round 2: Big ideas compared
rounds.intro: Similar words can hide very different ideas. Decide what sets neighboring concepts apart.

questions.q: Which pairing of teachers and traditions fits?
questions.scene: Teacher A: 'Each person has an unchanging inner self that is ultimately identical with ultimate reality.' Teacher B: 'What we call a self is a changing bundle of parts with no permanent core.'
choices: A: Theravada Buddhist; B: Advaita Vedanta
A: Advaita Vedanta; B: Buddhist
A: Jain; B: Advaita Vedanta
A: Jain; B: Buddhist
questions.why: Advaita Vedanta teaches atman is Brahman, while Buddhists teach anatta, no permanent self. Jains also teach an eternal soul (jiva) but do not identify it with Brahman, so A is not Jain.

questions.q: Muslims stress that associating partners with God (shirk) is the gravest wrong. Which concept does this protect?
choices: Covenant at Sinai
Karma
Tawhid, God's oneness
Advaita, the non-dual unity of self and Brahman
questions.why: Tawhid is the central Islamic teaching that God is one and has no partners. Advaita also speaks of oneness, but of the identity of self and Brahman, not a creator distinct from creation.

questions.q: In the 1500s, Protestant Reformers such as Luther stressed justification by faith alone. Which statement best describes the Catholic response at the Council of Trent?
choices: People earn salvation through good works apart from God's grace, so faith is secondary
Faith plays no role, because salvation is decided by works
Everyone is predestined to an outcome regardless of faith
Grace comes first, and faith works through good deeds and the sacraments
questions.why: Trent taught that grace comes first and that people cooperate with it. Reformers also taught that good works follow from faith, so the debate was about how faith, grace and works relate, not whether works matter.

questions.q: A student writes that Hindus and Buddhists both seek liberation from rebirth. Which distinction is accurate?
choices: Moksha is release of the atman; nirvana is the ending of craving without a permanent self
Hindus call it nirvana and teach no self; Buddhists call it moksha and teach an eternal atman
Buddhists reject rebirth, while Hindus accept it
The two ideas are identical in every school
questions.why: Both traditions teach samsara and a path out of it, but they define the goal differently, and each tradition has internal variety. The terms are not simply swappable.

questions.q: Which statement best compares Jain and Buddhist approaches to non-harm?
questions.scene: A Jain monk sweeps the ground ahead of him to avoid crushing insects. A Theravada monk also keeps the precept against killing.
choices: Buddhists forbid harm to insects, while Jains consider only the intention behind an act
Jains avoid even unintended harm, and Buddhists give intention central weight
Only Jains believe in rebirth
Only Buddhists practice non-violence
questions.why: Both traditions value ahimsa. Jain practice is stricter and sees all living beings as having souls. Buddhists focus on the intention behind an act, so the two are often mixed up.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is called the 'Seal of the Prophets'. What does this phrase express?
choices: He is regarded as divine, the son of God, and an object of worship
He was the first prophet, before Adam
He is the final prophet after Abraham, Moses and Jesus
He is the final avatar of Vishnu
questions.why: Muslims teach that prophets came to every people and that Muhammad completes the line. Some groups, such as Bahá'ís, teach progressive revelation with later messengers, and Muslims in general do not accept that.

questions.q: Which concept is described?
questions.scene: A rabbi explains that Jewish identity involves a relationship with God shaped by commitments, from God's promises to Noah and Abraham to the giving of the commandments at Sinai.
choices: Hukam, the divine order in Sikhism
Tawhid, the oneness of God
Moksha, liberation from rebirth
Berit, covenant
questions.why: Berit means covenant, a binding relationship with obligations on both sides. Hukam is Sikh divine order and moksha is a Hindu goal, so they do not describe Sinai.

questions.q: Which pairing of tradition and view of ultimate reality is most accurate?
choices: Advaita Vedanta: Brahman identical with atman; Islam: one transcendent creator
Advaita Vedanta: a creator distinct from all souls; Islam: ultimate reality identical with the self
Daoism: a personal creator who issues commandments; Judaism: an impersonal force
Theravada Buddhism: an eternal creator God; Sikhism: no divine reality
questions.why: Advaita is one school of Vedanta, and other Hindu schools see God as distinct from souls. In Islam the Creator is wholly distinct from creation. The Dao is generally described as an impersonal source, and Sikhs teach one God.

rounds.title: Round 3: Practice, calendar and sacred space
rounds.intro: Religions are lived as well as believed. Match the rituals, festivals and places to their traditions.

questions.q: Which pilgrimage is described?
questions.scene: Pilgrims wear simple white garments, circle the Kaaba in Mecca seven times and later stand together on the plain of Arafat.
choices: Kumbh Mela
Camino de Santiago
Hajj
Pilgrimage to Bodh Gaya
questions.why: These are rites of the Hajj, which Muslims who are able are expected to perform once. Kumbh Mela is a Hindu gathering at sacred rivers, and Bodh Gaya is a Buddhist site.

questions.q: Which statement about fasting is accurate?
choices: Yom Kippur lasts a whole lunar month, while Ramadan is a single fast of about a day
Ramadan is a single fast of about 25 hours, while Yom Kippur is a daily fast lasting a lunar month
In Islam, Lent is the fast that runs from dawn to sunset throughout a lunar month
Ramadan is a daily dawn-to-sunset fast for a month; Yom Kippur is one fast of about 25 hours
questions.why: Muslims fast daily during Ramadan, and Jews fast once on Yom Kippur from sunset to nightfall. Lent is a Christian season of preparation before Easter, and fasting practices within it vary by church.

questions.q: Diwali season is observed by several Indian traditions. Which pairing is accurate?
choices: Jains remember Mahavira's liberation; Sikhs mark Bandi Chhor Divas
Jains mark Buddha's enlightenment; Sikhs mark the birth of Guru Nanak in spring
Both Jains and Sikhs mark Rama's return to Ayodhya
Sikhs remember Mahavira's liberation; Jains mark the founding of the Khalsa
questions.why: Many Hindus link Diwali to Rama's return and to Lakshmi. Jains and Sikhs have their own stories for the same season. Guru Nanak's birthday is a separate festival close in time, which causes mix-ups.

questions.q: In Theravada tradition, Vesak (Visakha Puja) commemorates which events?
choices: The Buddha's first sermon only
Buddha's birth, enlightenment, death
The birth of Mahavira
The arrival of Buddhism in China under the Han
questions.why: Theravada communities mark all three events on one full-moon day. The first sermon is remembered on a different holy day, and some Mahayana communities celebrate the Buddha's birth on a separate date.

questions.q: Which practice and principle are described?
questions.scene: At a gurdwara, visitors of every background sit in rows on the floor and share the same vegetarian meal, prepared and served by volunteers.
choices: Iftar, a meal that breaks the Ramadan fast
Dana, giving food to monastics
Langar, the Sikh community kitchen
The Seder, a Passover meal that retells the Exodus
questions.why: Langar is a Sikh community kitchen that welcomes everyone, reflecting equality and seva. Dana is Buddhist giving, often directed to monastics, so it does not match.

questions.q: Which pairing of day and observance is accurate?
choices: Jewish Shabbat runs Saturday sunrise to sunset; Muslims worship in congregation on Sunday
Shabbat is Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall; Muslims hold Jumu'ah on Friday
Shabbat is on Sunday; Christians worship on Friday
Jumu'ah is on Saturday; Shabbat is Friday morning only
questions.why: Shabbat begins at sundown on Friday. Many Christians gather on Sunday to mark the Resurrection, and Muslims hold the weekly Friday midday prayer, which is not a day of mandated rest.

questions.q: Which set of rites of passage is correctly matched?
choices: Bar/Bat Mitzvah: Jewish; Upanayana: Hindu thread; Confirmation: Catholic
Upanayana: Sikh initiation; Amrit Sanchar: Hindu thread ceremony
Pabbajja: Jewish coming of age; Bar Mitzvah: Buddhist ordination as a novice
Aqiqah: Hindu thread ceremony; Confirmation: Jewish coming of age
questions.why: Amrit Sanchar is the Sikh initiation into the Khalsa, and Pabbajja is going forth as a Buddhist novice. Aqiqah is a Muslim ceremony for a newborn. Upanayana is performed in some Hindu communities.

questions.q: Why does Passover always fall in spring in the Northern Hemisphere, while Ramadan moves through all the seasons?
choices: Both use purely solar calendars, but Ramadan is adjusted by tradition to fall at varying times
The Jewish calendar is lunisolar with a leap month; the Islamic has 12 lunar months, no leap month
The Jewish calendar is solar and the Islamic calendar is lunisolar
Both are purely lunar, but Passover is fixed by priestly decree
questions.why: Adding a leap month keeps the Jewish calendar aligned with the seasons. The Islamic calendar is purely lunar, so Ramadan shifts about 11 days earlier each year in the solar calendar.

rounds.title: Round 4: History, schisms and branches
rounds.intro: Traditions grow, divide and spread. Sort out who split from whom, and how religions traveled.

questions.q: Which statement describes the main Sunni and Shia positions on leadership after Muhammad's death in 632?
choices: Shia held that the community elects the caliph, while Sunnis held that Ali's descendants have divinely designated authority
Sunnis held that only Muhammad's descendants may lead, while Shia held that leaders are elected
Both groups agree that Ali was the first caliph
Sunnis accepted caliphs chosen by consultation; Shia hold Muhammad designated Ali and his descendants
questions.why: This is the root of the Sunni/Shia divide. The first option reverses the two positions. Ali did become the fourth Sunni caliph, but only after Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman.

questions.q: Which pairing of Buddhist tradition and emphasis is accurate?
choices: Theravada: Pali Canon, Sri Lanka; Mahayana: bodhisattva ideal, East Asia; Vajrayana: tantric methods, Tibet
Theravada: tantric methods, strong in Tibet; Vajrayana: Pali Canon, strong in Sri Lanka
Mahayana: Pali Canon only; Theravada: bodhisattva ideal in East Asia
Vajrayana: based on the Vedas and strong in India; Mahayana: strong in Thailand and Sri Lanka, with the Pali Canon as its core
questions.why: These are broad generalizations, since every tradition has diversity, and Vajrayana grew out of Mahayana. Thailand and Sri Lanka are mainly Theravada, and Vajrayana is not based on the Vedas.

questions.q: Which statement about Christian divisions is accurate?
choices: In 1054, Protestants split from Rome over papal authority; in 1517, the Orthodox split from Constantinople over the filioque
In 1054 Rome and Constantinople split over papal authority and the filioque; in 1517 Luther began the Reformation
The Council of Nicaea in 325 separated Catholics from Orthodox
The Reformation and the Great Schism were the same event in 1054
questions.why: The Great Schism split Western and Eastern Christianity, with mutual excommunications in 1054. The Reformation came about 460 years later and created Protestant churches. Nicaea was a unifying council.

questions.q: Which Jewish movement is described?
questions.scene: A congregation holds that halakha (Jewish law) is binding and develops through rabbinic interpretation. It also accepts modern historical study of the texts and allows change through a legal process.
choices: Orthodox Judaism
Reform Judaism
Conservative (Masorti) Judaism
Reconstructionist Judaism, led by Mordecai Kaplan
questions.why: Conservative Judaism combines a commitment to halakha with historical study. Orthodox Judaism generally holds that halakha comes from Sinai, and Reform emphasizes individual interpretation of ethics over strict legal obligation.

questions.q: Which pairing about origins is accurate?
choices: Guru Nanak founded Jainism; Mahavira founded Sikhism
Rishabhanatha is the 24th Jain Tirthankara and a contemporary of the Buddha; Kabir founded Sikhism in Punjab
Mahavira was the first Jain teacher; Sikhism began in Bengal
Mahavira, a contemporary of the Buddha, is the 24th Tirthankara; Guru Nanak founded Sikhism in Punjab
questions.why: Jains see their tradition as eternal, with Mahavira as the last of 24 Tirthankaras, and Rishabhanatha as the first. Kabir's verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib, but Kabir did not found Sikhism.

questions.q: Who do Bahá'ís regard as the founder-prophet of their faith, which emerged in 19th-century Persia?
choices: Bahá'u'lláh, who followed the Báb as forerunner
The Báb alone, with no later figure
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, founder of the Ahmadiyya movement
Guru Nanak
questions.why: Bahá'ís teach that Bahá'u'lláh fulfilled the Báb's promise of a coming messenger and that revelation is progressive. Ahmadiyya is a separate 19th-century movement that began in Punjab.

questions.q: Which statement about how religions spread along trade routes is best supported?
choices: Buddhism reached China by sea from Japan, and Islam reached West Africa along the Silk Road
Buddhism entered China along Silk Road routes; Islam reached Southeast Asia through Indian Ocean trade
Hinduism spread to Europe along the Silk Road, and Buddhism reached Arabia by sea in the 7th century as the main religion of Arabian traders
Judaism spread mainly by missionary kings in the Americas
questions.why: Merchants, monks and travelers carried religions along Silk Road and Indian Ocean routes. Buddhism came to China from the west, and Japan received it from the mainland. Islam reached West Africa mainly across trans-Saharan trade routes.

questions.q: Twelver, Ismaili and Zaydi Shia all honor Ali but differ on the line of imams. Which statement is accurate?
choices: All Shia groups recognize exactly twelve imams
Twelvers trace the imamate through Ismail, son of Ja'far al-Sadiq, while Ismailis believe the twelfth imam is in hiding, and Zaydis accept it too
Twelvers follow twelve imams, the last in occultation; Ismailis follow Ismail; Zaydis follow Zayd ibn Ali as fifth imam
Zaydis believe the twelfth imam is in occultation, while Twelvers follow Zayd ibn Ali
questions.why: Succession disputes created different Shia branches. Ismailis split over Ismail after Ja'far al-Sadiq, and Zaydis recognize Zayd as the fifth imam and do not teach a hidden twelfth imam.
